Introduction to cori.data.ipeds

introduction.Rmd

What is this data?

The Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS) is the annual survey the National Center for Education Statistics collects from every institution participating in federal student aid programs — roughly 6,000 colleges, universities and technical schools. Reporting is mandatory for participants, so IPEDS is a near-census of American higher education rather than a sample.

NCES distributes it as about a dozen separate survey files per year, each with its own grain and identifier conventions. This package harmonizes four of them:

Measure Getter NCES file Grain of the source file
Institutional characteristics get_institutions() HD{year} One row per institution
Degrees conferred get_degrees() C{year}_A Institution × CIP × award level × major number
Students completing get_completers() C{year}_C Institution × award level category
Graduation rates get_graduation_rates() GR{year} Institution × cohort type × status

Not covered: enrollment (EF), finance (F), staff (S), admissions (ADM), student financial aid (SFA) and outcome measures (OM). Those are separate IPEDS surveys with their own grains, and nothing here reads them.

Data is available at the county and institution levels from 2010 to the present, with two exceptions: completers begin in 2012, because NCES published no C_C file before that, and graduation rates lag the other surveys by about a year.

Quick start 

library(cori.data.ipeds)
# See all available variables, which survey they come from, and their coverage
get_ipeds_codebook()

All four data getters follow the same signature, get_*(geography, geoids, years, variables, unitids), and at county level return tidy (long) format: geoid | year | variable | value | agg_var | survey. agg_var carries the denominator where the variable is a rate or share, so counties can be rolled up correctly.

# Institutional presence and composition
institutions <- get_institutions(geoids = "33009", years = 2024)

# Degrees conferred
degrees <- get_degrees(geoids = "33009", years = 2024)

# Students completing — distinct from degrees, see below
completers <- get_completers(geoids = "33009", years = 2024)

# Completion outcomes
grad_rates <- get_graduation_rates(geoids = "33009", years = 2012:2023)

get_ipeds() is the general getter for pulling across all four functions in one call:

# Everything known about one county in one year
get_ipeds(geoids = "33009", years = 2024)

Two levels: county and institution

geography selects the geographic unit, the same as in other cori.data packages. IPEDS is collected from institutions rather than places, so the finest unit available here is the institution itself — every record carries coordinates, address, city and county — and county output aggregates those points.

# County level (default): tidy long, one row per geoid x year x variable
get_degrees(geoids = "33009", years = 2024)

# Institution level: wide, one row per institution and the survey's own
# dimensions -- CIP code, award level, cohort type
get_degrees(geography = "institution", geoids = "33009", years = 2024)

The county level is an aggregation restricted to degree-granting institutions, with NCES’s grand-total rows, second majors and certificates already excluded. The institution level is deliberately unfiltered — it keeps everything NCES publishes, including the CIP detail, so you can aggregate on your own terms.

Two things to know before using the output:

  • variables applies to the county level only. At institution level the output is wide, so select columns after the call.
  • Absence is represented by no row. A county with no degree-granting institution does not appear in the county output. Start joins from a full county list, or the counties the question is about drop out silently.

What this package changes

Both levels differ from the raw NCES files in the same ways:

  • Canonical names. COUNTYCD becomes geoid, AWLEVEL becomes ed_level, and so on. get_ipeds_codebook() is the mapping, and it drives the ETL rather than merely documenting it.
  • Sentinels become NA. NCES codes “not reported”, “not applicable” and “not available” as -1, -2 and -3. Left as integers they silently corrupt any mean.
  • Identifiers stay character. unitid is zero-padded to six digits and cipcode to "xx.xxxx", so CIP families 01 through 09 keep their leading zero and still join to the SOC crosswalk.
  • Derived flags are added. is_public, is_4yr, is_degree_granting, is_hbcu, is_tribal and others are computed from sector_code and the NCES status codes.

Decoding categorical variables

Much of IPEDS is categorical, and the institution level returns those columns as the bare integers NCES publishes. The codebook’s codes column carries the value labels.

cb <- get_ipeds_codebook()

# Categorical variable labels
cb[nzchar(cb$codes), c("variable", "label")]

# What do sector_code's numbers mean?
cb$codes[cb$variable == "sector_code"]
#> "0 = Administrative unit only; 1 = Public, 4-year or above; ..."

Only codes that actually occur in the published data are listed, and the NCES sentinels are absent because the ETL converts them to NA.

Mapping programs to occupations

get_cip_soc_crosswalk() returns the NCES crosswalk from CIP program codes to SOC occupation codes, which turns the institution level’s CIP detail into a workforce measure.

xw <- get_cip_soc_crosswalk("2020")   # CIP 2020 to SOC 2018, for years 2020+
xw <- get_cip_soc_crosswalk("2010")   # CIP 2010 to SOC 2010, for 2010-2019

The relation is many-to-many, so joining it to completions multiplies rows. Collapse to a distinct CIP set before joining, or any sum afterwards is inflated.

Filtering by geography 

# Specific counties
degrees <- get_degrees(geoids = c("33009", "33011"), years = 2015:2024)

# A whole state, via the institution table's st_abbr. This lists only counties
# that contain an institution; start from a full county list before joining
# other data.
mt_counties <- get_institutions(geography = "institution", years = 2024) |>
  dplyr::filter(st_abbr == "MT") |>
  dplyr::distinct(geoid) |>
  dplyr::pull(geoid)

get_degrees(geoids = mt_counties, years = 2024)

# Specific institutions, by IPEDS unit ID
get_degrees(geography = "institution", unitids = "182670", years = 2024)

Rural vs. nonrural comparison 

library(dplyr)

county_degrees <- get_degrees(geography = "county", years = 2024)

rural_definition <- ruraldefinitions::cbsa_2023 |> select(geoid, is_rural)

county_comparison <- county_degrees |>
  filter(variable == "count_degrees_total") |>
  left_join(rural_definition, by = "geoid") |>
  filter(!is.na(is_rural)) |>
  group_by(year, is_rural) |>
  summarize(total_degrees = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

print(county_comparison)

Understanding agg_var

Variables that are rates or shares include an agg_var column — the weight needed to aggregate correctly across counties. For graduation rates it is the adjusted cohort; for degree shares it is total degrees conferred, so value * agg_var recovers a raw count.

An unweighted mean gives a 40-student county the same weight as a 40,000-student one:

rates <- get_graduation_rates(geography = "county", years = 2023)

rates |>
  filter(variable == "grad_rate_150pct") |>
  summarize(
    weighted   = sum(value * agg_var, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(agg_var, na.rm = TRUE),
    unweighted = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

Counting conventions

The institution tables are unfiltered because the right filter depends on the question. Three NCES conventions will inflate a naive sum:

  • cipcode == "99.0000" is each institution’s grand total across programs, included alongside the per-program rows.
  • major_num == 2 is the second major of a double-majoring student.
  • Certificates are not degrees. ed_level spans certificates through doctorates; the county variables count codes 3, 5, 7, 17, 18 and 19 only.

The first two together inflate a 2024 national degree count from 4.14 million to 8.46 million. The county getters apply all three already, so this matters only when aggregating the institution tables directly.

Coverage caveats

get_ipeds_codebook() carries a notes field per variable recording vintage caveats. These are the ones that most often change an answer.

Graduation rates lag the other surveys by about a year.

Transfer-out reporting is effectively optional. A county-year where no institution reported a transfer-out row is omitted rather than published as zero, so transfer_out_rate is absent for roughly a quarter of the county-years that do have a graduation rate. A value of 0 is a reported zero, not missing data.

Award level codes changed inside the covered period. ed_level code 1 runs 2010–2019 and is replaced by codes 20 and 21 from 2020; award_level_category code 1 is likewise replaced by 11 and 12. All are sub-associate certificates and all are excluded from degree aggregations, so county variables are unaffected, but aggregating certificates from the institution tables requires using the right code for the year.

Completer variables are not additive across levels. A student earning a bachelor’s and a master’s in the same year is counted at both.

Geography is the institution’s, not the student’s. County assignment comes from the institution’s address, so commuting and online enrollment both appear as production in the campus county.

Carnegie classification is the 2000 edition and is NA for roughly half of all institution-years: NCES codes institutions outside the Carnegie universe as -2, which the ETL converts to NA.
